Granted by the sectioned rune. The weapon has separated into linked segments joined by fine chain.

The weapon gains the reach trait. You take a −2 circumstance penalty to Strikes against adjacent creatures (applied automatically when a target is within 5 feet). When you critically hit with the unfolded weapon, the target takes 1d4 persistent bleed damage.

Refolding the weapon is an Interact action — delete this effect, or use the Sectioned: Unfold / Refold macro.

Your sectioned weapon separates into linked segments joined by fine chain, or draws back together into a single solid weapon.

Effect Toggle the Effect: Sectioned (Unfolded) effect on yourself. While unfolded, the weapon gains the reach trait, you take a −2 circumstance penalty to Strikes against adjacent creatures, and critical hits deal 1d4 persistent bleed damage.

description.gm:
Continuity. Successor to FlickerStitch's Sectioned Stave of Soothe (Rank 2) (item 5, 410 gp): charges instead of one casting a day, plus his two psi cantrips.

Item 6 / 230 gp is the official curve for a staff topping out at 2nd-rank spells (Librarian Staff 225 gp, Staff of Control 230 gp). It sits one level above him at 5, which is normal for a signature item.

Upgrade path: Flicker's Staff (Sectioned) — item 8, adds 3rd-rank soothe and the sectioned rune.
description.value:
Two feet of driftwood ash off Junker's Edge, sanded pale by the sea and mended in four places with copper wire and boot-leather. FlickerStitch made it the way he was made: out of parts nobody wanted, stitched together, working anyway.

Every clear inch of the shaft is covered in tiny, painstaking goblin script — names, mostly, written small so that more will fit. He will tell you it is a list of everyone he has patched up. It is also a list of everyone he has decided to keep.

The brass cage at the head holds nothing at all. Whatever was set in it washed up somewhere else, or never existed; a pale light gathers there regardless when the staff is used — the same flicker that sits behind his eyes.

"Staff not magic. Staff is REMEMBERING. Flicker write down who not-die, and then they keep on not-dying. Is a system."

description.gm:
Upgrade of Flicker's Staff (item 6, 230 gp): adds 3rd-rank soothe, a +1 weapon potency rune, and the sectioned rune.

Price 450 gp (item-8 staff, against Staff of Healing (Greater) at 470 gp) + 35 gp (potency) + 250 gp (sectioned) = 735 gp. Item level stays 8 — the highest of the staff's 3rd-rank spells (8), the sectioned rune (6), and +1 potency (2).

Flagged as a specific magic item so the system leaves the authored price alone instead of recomputing it from the runes. The potency rune is set in item data, so the +1 to attack rolls is automatic; sectioned can't go in the property-rune list (it isn't a system rune), so it lives in the name, the description, and the module's effect.

In Foundry: run the Sectioned: Unfold / Refold macro and pick this staff at the prompt.

description.gm:
Upgrade of Flicker's Staff (Sectioned): adds a striking rune and 4th-rank spells.

Price 900 gp (item-10 staff, the curve for 4th-rank spells) + 35 gp potency + 65 gp striking + 250 gp sectioned = 1,250 gp. Item 10.

Ranked spells follow The Oscillating Wave's granted list exactly — breathe fire, blazing bolt, fireball, ice storm — so everything on the staff is already on FlickerStitch's spell list.

+1 potency allows one property rune, which sectioned occupies. Striking and potency are set in item data and automate; sectioned uses the module's effect.

description.gm:
Upgrade of Flicker's Staff (Striking): adds a flaming rune and 5th-rank spells.

Price 1,800 gp (item-12 staff, the curve for 5th-rank spells) + 935 gp potency +2 + 65 gp striking + 250 gp sectioned + 500 gp flaming = 3,550 gp. Item 12.

Potency +2 is required, not optional — a weapon holds as many property runes as its potency value, and this staff carries two (sectioned and flaming). That upgrade is most of the price jump.

Flaming is a real system rune and sits in the property list, so its 1d6 fire and 1d10 persistent fire on a crit are automated. Only sectioned needs the module's effect.
